title: Imitation of God's Mercy
english: Our heavenly perfect one is, and he does not mean that we should strive to become like God when he says we should become merciful like the Father, because it is impossible for us to become like the Father, being creatures and having come from non-being, out of that which does not exist.

Rather, we are to look at the good deeds of our heavenly Father and do good things for his sake, not for human recognition, so that we will receive our reward from him, and not from humans, just as we, being one only-begotten Son by nature and true, become sons by grace of the one who called us.

We are called gods by grace, being humans, and not by nature, and we become merciful like God, not by being equal to him, but by imitating his kindness, for it is not our discovery to do good, but God's, and we are to extend kindness to all people, without discriminating, just as God does.

This is the only way we can become imitators of him, and it is by serving each other from him, as also in all his Epistles, speaking about these things, in which there are some things that are hard to understand.
For Christ speaks in him, and you, beloved, knowing beforehand, will guard yourselves, so that you will not be led astray by the error of the lawless and fall from your own steadfastness.

You must turn away from those who come to you in the name of Christ but are actually deceivers, for our Lord Jesus Christ has given us a command for our safety and salvation, warning us to beware of those who come to us in sheep's clothing but inside are ravenous wolves (Matthew 7:15).

The Lord commands us not to become like a horse and a mule, so that we do not imitate their irrationality, and he says 'Become merciful like the Father', which means we should do good things, looking at his good deeds, and not for human recognition.
By following this command, we will be able to extend kindness to all people, without discriminating, and receive our reward from God, not from humans.
As the apostle Paul says, some things in his Epistles are hard to understand, but it is certain that they are full of wisdom from above, for Christ speaks in him.

Therefore, knowing beforehand, you will guard yourselves, so that you will not be led astray by the error of the lawless and fall from your own steadfastness, and you must turn away from those who come to you in the name of Christ but are actually deceivers.

title: Deception and Love
english: We must be careful not to be deceived by anyone, for many will come in my name claiming to be the Christ and will deceive many.
Paul cries out, warning us to beware of those who are evil workers of the faith in the Lord Jesus, referring to them as 'dogs'.
God is light, and there is no darkness in him; in fact, God exists as light in essence.
Those who walk in virtues in him will truly become light, while darkness represents evil, a concept that is also illustrated through the Jews.
The Lord himself taught us about love, saying that 'no one has greater love than to lay down his life for his friends' (John 15:13).
This commandment of love is not new, but rather an old one that we have had from the beginning, and it is the word that we heard from the beginning.
The Lord promised this commandment through the prophets, saying that it is not an elder or an angel, but the Lord himself who saves us because he loves us and cares for them.
I am writing to you, fathers, and to you, young men, and to you, children.
When considering age, it is the inner man that matters, for the evangelist did not write to infants, but rather to those who have come to spiritual maturity.
In this context, young men are those who have come to spiritual manhood, and elders are those who have attained wisdom, while infants are those who have just believed in Christ.
We are instructed not to love the world, nor the things in the world, for if anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him.

translator_notes: The text appears to be a fragment, starting mid-sentence with 'Again, see that no one deceives you…' but this is not included in the current translation.
The Greek text contains a quote from John 15:13, which is included in the translation as 'no one has greater love than to lay down his life for his friends'.

title: Faith and Worldly Distractions
english: The things of this world are either vanity or uselessness, for some people do not preserve them for any useful purpose, but rather act foolishly, as they are seen acting without a purpose.
The present life is marked by superfluous and useless distractions, as well as the filthiness of worldly desires.
The disciple of Christ warns us, saying, 'Do not love the world or the things in the world' (1 John 2:15), and 'if our heart does not condemn us, we have confidence towards God' (1 John 3:21).
As long as we are on this path of life, which is a journey taken by all people, we should receive and not disregard the reminder from our conscience.
However, if we disregard and run past our life, our conscience will accuse you before the judge, make you subject to the verdict of the one judging, and subject you to unbearable punishments.

We would not have suffered these things if we had obtained favor towards the opponent by receiving rebukes with favor, as the divine evangelist John also reminds us that if our conscience does not condemn us, we have confidence towards God (1 John 3:21).
Our faith is the victory that has conquered the world, and it is the one who believes that Jesus is the Son of God who conquers the world (1 John 5:5).
Neither Greek, nor Jew, nor heretic can stand against this faith once the victorious works of our faith have been brought forth.
Beloved, making every effort to write to you about our common salvation, I had a necessity to write to you, exhorting you to struggle for the faith once delivered to the saints.

While simultaneously safeguarding us and condemning the heretics, the Holy Spirit, through the prophets and apostles, has forewarned us about the rise of heretics, making us more secure in our faith, so that we will not be caught off guard by their clever arguments.
We are not to be distracted by the heretics' deception and wicked faith.
